reconstruction.scope: Gate of Felicity (Babussaade) and the connected mapped arcade wings only, third authored member of18 required Topkapi Palace structures. Low cream gatehouse, actual open lower route, projecting four-column canopy with wide eaves, polygonal lead drum and faceted dome/five gold finials, pale front shafts, grey-green rear/wing columns and pointed arcades, rear open balustrade and occupied stone floor. Fine ceiling scenes/calligraphy/tughra, furnishings, visitors, security equipment and the independent Audience Chamber remain outside this model. Long connected wings use a simple repeated arcade rhythm and standard-ground-following floor/roof controls; exact bay inventory and historical thresholds are approximate.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Picture-led working wing eaves about6m above local occupied floor, central octagonal drum to8.15m, faceted lead dome to11.5m and main finial to12.95m; canopy shafts to5.15m and wing/rear shafts to3.65m. Portal clear width3.1m, spring2.7m/rise0.75m above local grade. These heights, eave curves, arch profiles, shaft spacing, gold finial shapes and paneled-door proportions are approximate visualization geometry, not surveyed dimensions, exact current condition or engineering/access certification. Recognition comes from the dome, deep columned canopy, real route and side arcades; fine painted ceiling art is excluded.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Existing standard PMTiles/Mapzen terrain retained. Native front-path control internal[3.8,23] sets Y0; rear control[3.8,-12] defines the modest through-passage cross slope. Connected wings follow nine front-ground samples along their length, preserving original terrain outside the tightly occupied mapped parent. Roof/floor subdivisions follow those controls; columns remain upright. This is an explicit approximate adaptation to the host terrain, whose eastern wing drops several metres. No broad courtyard slab, terrain flattening, independent-building replacement or water cutout. Original native terrain, footprint ownership, front-facing entry and approximate exterior contact were visually inspected2026-10-21 and accepted. The independent Audience Chamber procedural shell meets the rear boundary and obscures a distant rear view; the authored rear portico remains intact and is inspected from inside its own footprint. Exact historical wing levels and host terrain accuracy remain approximate.
